sourceMutationGate.scope: Successful git diff --exit-code compares the working tree with the index. It does not enumerate untracked artifacts or independently compare staged content with HEAD.

jobs.scope: Build and deterministic checks only; no separate packed-install or native Codex registration step in the fast workflow.

expectedUnitScope: 272 tests discovered in each job. Windows runs all 272. Other jobs pass 260 and skip the same 12: seven Windows/PowerShell automation tests and five Windows 8.3 alias tests. All 30 edit_block tests pass on each runner.
nativeCodexScope: The matrix runs the actual platform-native Codex CLI 0.160.1 from a test-owned npm prefix against synthetic configuration, then exercises two registered-command MCP SDK rounds. Its reported installedEntry is false. Packaged installed-entry MCP verification is separate. There are no actual Codex agent/model tool calls, and no real user configuration changes.

methodology: Only read-only GitHub connector GET and job-log retrieval were used.
Raw decoded log strings were encoded directly to UTF-8 without normalization, preserving BOM and newline bytes returned by the connector.

Every job was inspected independently. Assertions bind run metadata, actual checkout hash, commit tree, full suite counts, installed groups, native executable evidence, and completed source-mutation step.
No tests, retries, cancellations, remote writes, or product repository mutations were performed for this audit.
limitations: This report audits hosted-run evidence, not the separate Windows native full-wrapper/fresh-extraction qualification.
Passing the bounded edit scenarios does not establish full Desktop Commander parity or broader DCP acceptance.
The hosted source-mutation command checks working tree versus index, not untracked files or a separate staged-content comparison.
